Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo today — that was helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our side so we can scope an evaluation: 

- Primary goal: reliably summarize multi-hour clinician notes (20k–75k tokens) while preserving key events and flags for downstream alerts.
- Secondary: extract structured fields (meds, procedures, timing) for analytics.
- Must-haves: deterministic redaction of PHI, configurable retention, and clear failure modes when truncation happens.

Two asks to help us decide on next steps: 1) recommended model(s) and expected accuracy trade-offs for full-note summarization vs chunking+stitching, and 2) a quick benchmark or exemplar prompts we can run on a small data sample (anonymized).

Happy to share a sanitized slice of records once we sign an NDA/PO. Can you share a proposed evaluation scope and any red flags we should know up front?

Best,

Ella — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise proposal for an initial ops-focused eval and known risks based on the customer goals. I'm attaching a 1-week pilot plan (spreadsheet) and a starter prompt set you can run locally.

High-level recommendation (short):
- Pilot with two paths in parallel: 1) native long-context model variant (32k+ context), 2) chunk-and-stitch using 8k model with overlap + structured merge logic.
- Start with Redwood long-context variants we benchmark for summarization fidelity (see benchmark_readme.md). For cost/latency trade-offs, include a quantized 70B variant as an economical baseline.

Immediate risks & mitigations:
- Truncation risk: if request exceeds KV-cache limits we will fallback to chunked pipeline. Add warning headers in metadata so downstream systems can flag potential loss of context.
- PHI leakage in prompts: we recommend local redaction pass pre-send + deterministic redaction filters in-edge.
- Quality regression: baseline with 50 'gold' prompts and exact-match F1 + ROUGE; auto-alert if overall ROUGE drops >6% vs baseline.

Attached: carelytics_long_context_eval_plan.xlsx, carelytics_prompt_set_v1.txt, benchmark_readme.md.

Next steps suggested:
1) NDA/PO so we can load a sanitized sample into a private evaluation workspace.
2) Redwood runs the 2-path pilot on 200 notes (you provide sanitized sample or we can run in a private pipeline).
3) 1-week bench + 3-day qualitative review to tune prompts and stitching logic.

I'll loop Connor for technical setup and Aditya for pricing/commits. If that works, can we lock a tentative pilot start date next Tue (7/28)?

Ella — quick technical notes to add more color on the two-path approach and specific model variants we recommend for Carelytics.

1) Long-context native (recommended for fidelity):
- Variant: redwood/rc-long-32k-v1 (attention-optimized, KV cache extended).
- Expected behavior: preserves cross-note event references and temporal ordering better than chunk-and-stitch; lower downstream hallucination for timeline reconstruction.
- Trade-offs: ~2–2.5x token cost vs 8k baseline; tail latency higher for very long notes (>45k tokens).

2) Chunk-and-stitch (recommended for cost control + fallback):
- Variant: redwood/rc-quant-70b-8k (4-bit quantized) with overlap 512 tokens and structured merge prompts.
- Expected behavior: cheaper, more predictable latency; stitching loses some cross-segment co-reference unless we augment with a retrieval pass of recent segments.

3) Summarization fidelity concerns & tests:
- Recommended eval metrics: ROUGE-L, BLEU (for short segments), and a custom event-F1 for clinical events. Add a manual spot-check for 25 complex notes focusing on event order and PHI redaction fidelity.

4) Truncation and graceful degradation:
- Proposal: add explicit \"context_truncated\":true metadata when we drop earlier tokens; return a short diagnostic summary of what was removed (top 3 named entities or timestamps) so downstream consumers can decide to show \"partial result\" or trigger a re-run.

5) Security & redaction:
- Run deterministic PHI-redaction before sending; use a hashed id mapping if downstream needs re-linking. We can run redaction in your VPC for compliance.

I can support the infra setup for a private evaluation cluster; Vanessa will take lead on schedule and commercials.

-Connor

Vanessa / Connor — quick clarifications: thanks for the plan.

1) 60k records: our corpus has many >50k notes. Truncation would be unacceptable for certain workflows (safety alerts). Is streaming + progressive summarization an option?
2) Diagnostic metadata with no PHI is fine — types and timestamps are exactly what we want.
3) Prompt templates: please include an example that highlights event extraction + timeline generation (we have in-house examples we can share).

Also: our legal would prefer any sandbox/eval to be in a private workspace with logs retained for 30 days and egress controls. Pricing is a gating question — do you have a rough pilot cost estimate for the two-path approach (200 notes)?

Ella
